intuition.title: Compare two acid-specific hydrothermal preparations
intuition.text: The study deliberately changes acid identity, initial pH and hydrothermal temperature to obtain two anatase colloids with similar primary sizes. Sample 1 uses acetic acid at pH 2 and 280 °C; sample 2 uses nitric acid at pH 1.9 and 250 °C. The authors interpret later solution-behavior differences in terms of surface structure; the prior facet study is cited, not independently remeasured here.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, 6, Introduction, Colloid Synthesis and surface discussion

intuition.title: Each size method describes a different object or estimator
intuition.text: TEM reports number-average projected particle dimensions; XRD reports volume-average coherent crystallite sizes. DLS measures solvated, aggregated hydrodynamic dimensions. AUC sizes calculated using bulk anatase density and later hydration-model core sizes are derived interpretations, not interchangeable direct particle measurements.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–5, Figures 1–5 and DLS/model discussion

intuition.title: Analytical pH reveals different aggregation responses
intuition.text: Both samples are already aggregated at pH 1 according to the authors. Sample 2 shows strong aggregation between pH 1.96 and 1.99, whereas sample 1 follows a different sedimentation trend despite similar zeta potentials below the point of zero charge. These pH settings characterize the prepared colloids; they do not create extra synthesis recipe–structure pairs.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–5, Figures 3–5 and DLS block

intuition.title: Hydration shells are a qualified model
intuition.text: The authors combine DLS and AUC under hard-sphere and negligible-charge assumptions to infer an apparent hydrated density. Their spherical anatase-core/water-shell illustration is explicitly inadequate for aggregates, and shape cannot be separated from hydration using AUC alone. The last model row is printed as sample 1 at pH 1.96 although related DLS/density and conclusion statements concern sample 2; the assignment remains unresolved.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 5–6, Equation 4, model list and limitations

intuition.title: A future combined method is not a performed experiment
intuition.text: Flow field-flow fractionation coupled to AUC is proposed as future work to disentangle size, shape, hydration and charge distributions. It is not an additional demonstrated preparation or measurement series in this contribution.

general_background.title: Solvent and a closed reaction environment
general_background.summary: A heated closed solvent environment changes solubility, transport and precursor conversion compared with an open vessel. Changes in solvent properties and dissolution followed by reprecipitation can alter the pathways available for nucleation and crystal growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
